title: UNION
description: UNION stacks the results of two SELECTs into one result set, automatically removing any exact duplicate rows. Write a query that returns a single combined list of full names (`first_name || ' ' || last_name`) covering both customers and employees.
hints: Both SELECTs must return the same number of columns, in compatible types - here, one text column each, built from first_name || ' ' || last_name in both customers and employees.
Select the concatenated full name from customers, put UNION on its own between the two queries, then select the same concatenated expression from employees.
expected_behavior: Returns one column of full names, combining customers and employees, with exact duplicates collapsed.
solution: SELECT first_name || ' ' || last_name FROM customers UNION SELECT first_name || ' ' || last_name FROM employees;
explanation: UNION is the SQL analog of combining two lists and calling set() on the result - if the exact same row appeared in both halves, you'd only see it once.
